YC startup logo colors over time

Is it just me or is every startup orange now? To find out, here's every YC startup's primary color by batch year:

2005

The long view

Share of each year's batch by logo color. The eight most common colors are shown; click a chip to show or hide any color. Batches before 2011 are small and sparsely archived, so early shares are noisy.

View as data table

Industry dress codes

How strongly each industry over- or under-indexes on a color, relative to the YC-wide base rate. Cell tint scales with the ratio; a printed ratio marks cells that differ significantly from the base rate. Highlights: consumer startups wear pink and red, healthcare wears cyan and conspicuously avoids black, and fintech won't wear the color of losses. Government and unspecified industries (45 companies) are excluded.

View as data table

Make a logo people want – startup outcomes by logo color

Is palette destiny? Among the 1,056 companies from batches 2005–2018, old enough for outcomes to have settled, azure-logo companies were acquired at roughly twice the rate of black-logo companies, and the gap holds within every era of that cohort. Black-logo companies were likelier to end up inactive. Read it as color marking a company's type and era, not changing its fate. Colors with fewer than 25 companies in the cohort are omitted; hover a row for the full breakdown. (Tiny-sample trivia: teal is 4% of companies but 3 of YC's 23 IPOs; Airbnb and DoorDash are both red.)
